title: GPU cage enforcement: latency-aware shard quotas and eviction playbook
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Goal: implement a ‘cage’ enforcement mechanism across the Dedicated GPU fleet that provides predictable throughput and tail-latency guarantees for reserved tenants while reducing noisy-neighbor impact on co-tenants. This ticket covers the enforcement layer (quota accounting, shard assignment), an eviction/playbook for overloads, and integration points with the autoscaler and Console observability.

Background: customers on Dedicated expect committed throughput and latency SLOs. Current soft-quota model reduces average interference but allows tail amplification when multiple tenants spike simultaneously. We need a stricter, latency-aware enforcement that: 1) bounds per-tenant interference; 2) surfaces actionable signals to the autoscaler and operator; 3) supports graceful degradation for best-effort tenants.

Scope: design and implement per-lane "shard quotas" (token-bucket style) surfaced at the serving gateway and enforced inside the runtime scheduler; a two-stage eviction/playbook for noisy tenants that prefers soft-preemption and graceful KV-cache shedding before hard eviction; instrumentation for p95/p99 latency attribution by tenant and lane; APIs for Console to set per-tenant enforcement profiles (strict|balanced|best-effort).

Non-goals: building the autoscaler itself (covered in ENG-90123) or tenant billing changes. This ticket integrates with those systems but focuses on enforcement logic and operator playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant shard-quotas implemented and release-gated under feature flag: quota enforcement active on 10% of fleet in alpha.
Service-level test harness shows p95 latency for reserved tenants does not increase by more than 10% under synthetic neighbor spikes (baseline: p95 < 120ms).
Eviction playbook executed end-to-end in staging: soft-preempt -> KV-cache shed -> hard eviction after configurable grace window, with clear audit logs and notifications to Console.
Autoscaler integration signals (queue-length, blocked-rates, eviction-count) emitted and validated in metrics pipeline (prometheus -> observability dashboard).
Console controls added: per-tenant enforcement profile and visualizations for evictions and quota throttles (docs and screenshots attached).
Runbook and operator checklist for noisy-neighbor incidents merged to docs and linked from Alert definitions.
implementation_notes: Quota model: per-tenant sliding token-bucket sized by reserved tokens/sec + burst credits. Tokens deducted on request acceptance at gateway; runtime enforces at scheduling boundary to prevent token overdraw under fast-path batching.

Latency-awareness: token costs weighted by estimated per-request GPU token cost (sequence length * model token multiplier). If p95 latency for a lane crosses threshold, enforcement tightens bucket refill for non-reserved tenants in that lane.
Shard assignment: deterministic hashing by tenant -> shard to improve cache locality. Rebalance windows are rate-limited to avoid cascading KV-cache misses.

Soft-preempt flow: mark requests from offending tenant as low-priority, start probe-shed (partial KV-drop for < 10% requests) to measure impact, escalate to full KV-cache shedding if no improvement, then perform hard eviction of tenant workloads when safety thresholds met.

Safety nets: minimum guaranteed capacity for bailouts, circuit-breaker to stop evictions if cloud region health is degraded, and a broker policy to migrate high-tier tenants to isolated lanes before eviction when capacity exists.
Metrics: per-tenant metrics (tokens_consumed, token_block_count, eviction_count, preempted_requests, p50/p95/p99 latency_by_tenant) emitted at 10s resolution for debugging and 1m for dashboards.
APIs: internal admin endpoints to query and adjust enforcement profiles; read-only Console endpoints for tenant owners. All admin endpoints require RBAC and audit logs (KMS/HSM context preserved).
rollout_plan: Alpha (feature-flag): enable for internal tenants only in a single AZ cluster. Run synthetic noisy-neighbor experiments and collect metrics for 7 days.
Canary: enable for 10% of Dedicated fleet with a mix of reserved and best-effort tenants. Monitor key signals and runbook alerts for 72h before expanding.
Gradual rollout: increase to 50% over two weeks, refine tuning parameters (burst windows, grace_period) from telemetry.
Global: flip default enforcement to 'balanced' for new reservations; allow tenants to opt-in to 'strict' for extra guarantee. Communicate changes to customers via Console and release notes.
Rollback: feature-flag off triggers immediate soft-release: marked preempted queues will drain; hard evictions will be reversed by rescheduling jobs to previous lanes.
test_plan: Unit tests for token accounting and refill logic (edge cases: clock skew, double-consumption).
Integration tests: gateway -> runtime enforcement path under realistic batching (mix of 1-4 requests per batch).
SLA simulation: replay production request traces with injected spikes from synthetic tenants; validate p95/p99 isolation claims.
Chaos tests: kill scheduler processes and simulate rebalance windows to measure cache miss amplification and recovery time.
Load tests: sustained 8 hour soak with mixed workloads to validate long-tail behavior and credit depletion scenarios.
